Cc: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@flowline.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo token export + a couple of clarifying questions

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the streaming example looked promising. Attached is a raw export (flowline_token_profile.csv) from our staging traffic for the last 7 days. A few quick items we couldn't get into the call: 

- Typical user flow: short chat-first queries (10–40 tokens) for tracking updates, plus async batch enrichment calls (1–2k tokens) when we generate shipment summaries.
- Peak pattern: we see short surges at 11:00 and 16:00 local where QPS spikes ~5–8x for ~3–6 minutes.
- Streaming: our mobile client expects an initial chunk within 150ms and then steady deltas; we can tolerate slightly higher tail but need sub-500ms 99th for interactive chat.

Questions for you:
1) Can Redwood guarantee routing to a streaming-capable instance when model is quantized?
2) What's the recommended capacity buffer for the 8x short crest vs steady-state?
3) Any gotchas with KV caching for mixed short/long requests?

Attaching the CSV and a simple SLO matrix (slo_matrix.xlsx). Happy to jump on a short follow-up; lunchtime PT works best for us.

— Liam
Lead, Platform Integrations
Flowline Logistics

Subject: Re: Post-demo token export + a couple of clarifying questions

Thanks, Liam — very helpful export. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so we have a clean checklist. Please correct anything I get wrong.

Recap (from your CSV & notes):
- Steady baseline: ~18 QPS, median request ~35 tokens, median response ~45 tokens.
- Peak crests: 5–8x baseline for short bursts (3–6 minutes), driven by scheduled ETL + mobile push windows.
- Long-batch path: ~1–2k tokens, ~3–5 QPS during off-peak windows (async enrichment).
- Streaming requirement: initial first-chunk target ~150ms, interactive 99p <500ms.

Clarifying asks (we'll need answers to these to produce an accurate capacity recommendation):
A) Do you have separate SLA tiers per endpoint (chat vs enrichment) or is it a single SLO today?
B) What fraction of traffic can be delayed up to 2s for batching (i.e., how much is batch-tolerant)?
C) Are you willing to accept a model fallback (larger quantization, slightly higher perplexity) during extreme crest events?

Preliminary operational guidance from Redwood eng (copied below):
- For mixed short/long workloads, enable prefix KV caching for short chats — that reduces per-token compute on repeated context by ~30–40%.
- Autoscale policy: maintain headroom for 6x baseline with burst-targeted slots to cover 95% of minutes; use on-demand burst capacity for the remaining tail minutes.
- Streaming-mode instances must be pinned to a streaming-capable kernel; quantized variants are supported but need validation per-model (we'll run a quick perf pass).

Proposed next steps:
1) Short follow-up (30 min) to collect: per-endpoint SLOs, % batch-tolerant traffic, and a canonical example of the 1–2k token enrichment payload.
2) Redwood perf pass: we'll run a rapid internal validation (48 hours) on your export to produce a recommended slot sizing + suggested reserved capacity.
3) Draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with timelines and optional Dedicated commit sizing.

Options for meeting tomorrow: Tue Jul 1 12:00 PT or Wed Jul 2 10:00 PT.

If that works we'll invite Sergio to cover burst/autoscale mechanics and Marissa for the cost estimate.

— Rafa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Following the ask — added a few configuration notes after a quick scan of the CSV: 

1) Recommended baseline slot: 4 vGPU slots targeting a mixed workload profile (short chat hot paths + 2k-token enrichments). Expect sustained baseline throughput ~20 QPS with headroom for 120 concurrent short sessions.
2) Burst strategy: 6x short crests covered by autoscale with pre-warmed lightweight burst slots; for the final 2x tail minutes use on-demand burst (higher cost but rare).
3) Streaming tuning: allocate 1–2 cores to network thread on streaming instances and reduce minibatch time to 0–50ms for chat-first; ensure the streaming kernel is validated with your quantized checkpoint.
4) KV cache: enable prefix caching for chat with 12-hour TTL — reduces RLHF-style repeated prompts cost.

Estimated quick numbers (very preliminary):
- Hosted (pure burst): expected average monthly spend ~$7k–$10k (depends on tail minutes).
- 3-month Dedicated cushion (small): ~$18k/month reserved + lower per-token cost; breakeven if you have >40% traffic sustained at 6x.

Next steps for us: run the Redwood perf pass (48 hrs) on the CSV -> we'll share a one-page slot-sizing + cost delta doc. I'll also attach a short validation checklist we run against streaming quantized kernels.

If Flowline confirms the SLOs in the invite we can finalize sizing during the call.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
